CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  (Notice No. N2M24-144)

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a special meeting of the Alhambra City Council will be held
on Friday, November 22, 2024, commencing at 10:30 a.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California pursuant to the order of the
Mayor of the City of Alhambra, the Alhambra City Charter, the Alhambra Municipal Code, and
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

An agenda of such special meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

Dated:  November 21, 2024
Notice No.  N2M24-144

  MISSION STATEMENT

  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and
  quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive
  business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our
  community.

Watch and listen to the meeting as follows:
Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://cityofalhambra-org.zoom.us/j/89463580715?pwd=tKhhaujWbobnFkY1v6OeJywPxsNw4S.1
Webinar ID: 894 6358 0715, Passcode: 281050
Or by telephone by dialing (833) 548-0276 (Toll Free) or (833) 548-0282 (Toll Free) or (877) 853-5257
(Toll Free) or (888) 475-4499 (Toll Free) or +1(719) 359-4580 or +1(309) 205-3325 or +1(253) 215-8782
or +1(346) 248-7799 or +1(646) 931-3860 or +1(301) 715-8592 or +1(312) 626-6799 or +1(646) 558-
8656 and entering Webinar ID: 894 6358 0715 and Passcode: 281050. Please Note: All members of
the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can proceed. If there are
technical difficulties with Zoom during the meeting, the meeting will proceed regardless.
Addressing the Council:
In person: Section 2.04.210 of the Alhambra Municipal Code establishes the procedures for addressing
the Council. Any person wishing to address the Council during the meeting should complete a Speaker
Request Card and submit it to the City Clerk so the City Council knows you wish to speak. When called
upon by the presiding officer, please step to the podium.
Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the “Raise
Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will unmute speakers
participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your time to speak.
Remarks are limited to 5 minutes; however, the presiding officer may either extend or reduce the
maximum time to such period of time as the Council may determine.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Council who refuses to stop speaking after his/her
time has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede the
progress of the City Council meeting who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such
behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers upon direction of the presiding officer.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or his/her designee, shall be Sergeant-at-Arms of the
Council meetings. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding
officer for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the Council meeting.

Persons Authorized to be Within Rail: No person, except City official or their designees, shall be
permitted within the rail in front of the Council Chamber without the express consent of the Council.

Agenda Tracking Numbers: All numbers listed in bold after the title of each Agenda item are City Clerk
tracking numbers that are used for filing and research purposes.

   AGENDA
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  November 22, 2024
  10:30 a.m.

  ROLL CALL:  Lee, Maza, Maloney, Andrade-Stadler, Pérez

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M24-144

The City Clerk hereby reports that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City
Council being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with
Section 54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

COUNCIL BUSINESS

1.  APPROVE ABSENCES: KATHERINE LEE & ROSS J. MAZA – F92-27, M2M24-203

  Sec. 12 of the Alhambra City Charter provides in pertinent part that an “elective office
  becomes vacant . . . if a member of the council . . . fails to attend the meetings of the
  council . . .of which he or she is a member for a like period (i.e., 30 consecutive days),
  without being excused therefrom by the council.” Due to the short notice for the
  scheduling of this morning’s meeting, Vice Mayor Lee and Councilmember Maza were
  unable to attend. Therefore, staff requests that the City Council vote to excuse the
  absences of Ms. Lee and Mr. Maza.

  Recommended Action:  City Council vote to excuse Vice Mayor Lee’s and
  Councilmember Maza’s absence from this morning’s special meeting. (M2M24-203)

2.  REAFFIRMATION OF SUPPORT FOR SB54 AND ASSERTION ALHAMBRA POLICE
  DEPARTMENT’S POLICIES ARE IN LINE WITH SB54 – F2M24-16, M2M24-204

  At the April 22, 2019 City Council meeting a group of students from Alhambra High
  School presented 'Immigration Resolution Regarding City's Sanctions" during the oral
  communications portion of the meeting. The Council requested the item be brought back
  for consideration on a future agenda. On June 10, 2019 staff presented information on
  Senate Bill 54, California's "Sanctuary State Law", and Alhambra Police Department
  policy. SB54 prohibits local law enforcement from sharing certain immigration status
  information with the Federal government (ΊCΕ), and also prohibits expending resources
  to detain or assist ICE with immigration enforcement. In addition, Alhambra Police
  Department was in full compliance with SB54 and has an Immigration Violations policy
  that is in compliance with SB54. The Council heard comments from the public on the
  item, and adopted a Minute Order (M2M19-158) to support the tenets of SB54, to assert
  that Alhambra Police Department’s current immigration policies were in line with SB54,
  and to encourage staff to return with a plan for community outreach on this topic with the
  goal of educating the public. On November 20, 2024, Mayor Sasha Renée Pérez
  requested staff call a Special Meeting of the City Council to reaffirm the previous support

  3
11-22-24
   for SB54, and reassert Alhambra Police Department’s current policies are in-line with
  SB54. If readopted, staff will distribute this information on our social media platforms and
  post it on the City’s website.

  Recommended Action:  City Council reaffirm support of SB54, and reassert
  Alhambra Police Department’s current policies are in line with SB54. (M2M24-204)

ADJOURNMENT

  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. If you would like to sign-up to receive the City Council meeting
agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at www.cityofalhambra.org and you
will be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the subscription service. Pursuant to
Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda items for regular meetings of the
Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to that meeting, will be made
available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City
meeting (including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-
5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK

  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  November 22, 2024
  10:30 a.m.

ROLL CALL: At 10:48 a.m., on Friday, November 22, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
ABSENT:  LEE, MAZA

Officials Present: Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Assistant
Police Chief Seki

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M24-144

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

COUNCIL BUSINESS

1.  APPROVE ABSENCES: KATHERINE LEE & ROSS J. MAZA – F92-27, M2M24-203

  Sec. 12 of the Alhambra City Charter provides in pertinent part that an “elective office becomes
  vacant . . . if a member of the council . . . fails to attend the meetings of the council . . .of which
  he or she is a member for a like period (i.e., 30 consecutive days), without being excused
  therefrom by the council.” Due to the short notice for the scheduling of this morning’s meeting,
  Vice Mayor Lee and Councilmember Maza were unable to attend. Therefore, staff requested
  that the City Council vote to excuse the absences of Ms. Lee and Mr. Maza.

  Action Taken: City Council excused Vice Mayor Lee’s and Councilmember Maza’s absence
  from this morning’s special meeting. (M2M24-203)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  MAZA, LEE

2.  REAFFIRMATION OF SUPPORT FOR SB54 AND ASSERTION ALHAMBRA POLICE
  DEPARTMENT’S POLICIES ARE IN LINE WITH SB54 – F2M24-16, M2M24-204

  At the April 22, 2019 City Council meeting, a group of students from Alhambra High School
  presented 'Immigration Resolution Regarding City's Sanctions" during the oral
  communications portion of the meeting. The Council requested the item be brought back for
  consideration on a future agenda. On June 10, 2019 staff presented information on Senate
  Bill 54, California's "Sanctuary State Law", and Alhambra Police Department policy. SB54
  prohibits local law enforcement from sharing certain immigration status information with the
  Federal government (ΊCΕ), and also prohibits expending resources to detain or assist ICE

   with immigration enforcement. In addition, Alhambra Police Department was in full compliance
  with SB54 and has an Immigration Violations policy that is in compliance with SB54. The
  Council heard comments from the public on the item, and adopted a Minute Order (M2M19-
  158) to support the tenets of SB54, to assert that Alhambra Police Department’s current
  immigration policies were in line with SB54, and to encourage staff to return with a plan for
  community outreach on this topic with the goal of educating the public. On November 20, 2024,
  Mayor Sasha Renée Pérez requested staff call a Special Meeting of the City Council to reaffirm
  the previous support for SB54, and reassert Alhambra Police Department’s current policies
  are in-line with SB54. If readopted, staff would distribute this information on our social media
  platforms and post it on the City’s website.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., provided a printout of
  California Government Code Section 7284, “California Values Act” to Council and discussed
  the law as well as the need to offer protections to immigrants in California.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke in support of SB54 and
  supported Council’s reaffirmation of their support to alleviate fear within the community. She
  motioned to reaffirm support. Councilmember MALONEY seconded the motion. Mr.
  MALONEY referred to Mr. McCammon’s handout and discussed the history of immigration in
  California and the United States as well as the history of political rhetoric to scapegoat recent
  immigrants. He spoke in support of SB54 and discussed his family’s history in which his mother
  was sent to a Japanese American incarceration camp during WWII. Mayor PÉREZ explained
  that her goal in this action was to reaffirm the City’s stance on assisting the immigrant
  population of Alhambra. Ms. PÉREZ and Assistant Chief SEKI discussed the Alhambra Police
  Department’s policies coinciding with SB54 and California Government Code Section 7284 as
  well as the Police Department’s ongoing effort to instill trust within the community. Ms. PÉREZ
  spoke regarding the potential uncertainty of national policy after President-elect Trump’s
  inauguration in January.

  Action Taken:  City Council reaffirmed support of SB54, and reasserted Alhambra
  Police Department’s current policies are in line with SB54. (M2M24-204)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  MAZA, LEE

ADJOURNMENT: At 11:08 a.m. there being no further business for the Council to transact, the
Mayor, with the consent of the City Council, adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
  by
  BRIANNA LAMB MCCARTHY
  ASSISTANT CITY CLERK
